verses.eng: Of the unrepentant. "If on the other hand those who shall receive mysteries of the mystery of the Ineffable and of the mysteries of the First Mystery, turn and sin and come out of the body without having repented, then they will be even as those will be who have transgressed and not repented. Their dwelling also is in the midst of the jaws of the dragon of the outer darkness and they will perish and be Nawan-existent for ever. For this cause have I said to you: All men who shall receive the mysteries, if they knew the time when they come
out of the body, would watch themselves and not sin, in order that they may inherit the Light-kingdom for ever."
When then the Saviour had said this to his disciples, he said to them: Understand you in what manner I speak with you?"

Marayam interprets from a former saying. Marayam answered and said: "Yea, my Adanay, with precision have I precisely followed all the words which you have said. Concerning this word then you have spoken to us aforetime: 'If the house-holder knew at what hour in the night the thief comes to break into the house, he would keep awake and not suffer the man to break into his house.'"
When then Marayam had said this, the Saviour said: Well said, you spiritual Marayam. This is the word."

The Saviour continued again and said to his disciples: "Now, therefore, herald you to all men who shall receive mysteries in the Light, and speak to them, saying: Keep watch over yourselves and sin not, lest you heap evil on evil and go out of the body without having repented and become strangers to the Light-kingdom for ever."
When the Saviour had said this, Marayam answered and said: "My Adanay, great is the compassion of those mysteries which forgive sins at every time."

If even men on earth are compassionate, how much more then the highest mysteries? The Saviour answered and said to Marayam in the midst of the disciples: "If to-day a king who is an man of the world, gives a gift to men of his like, and also forgives murderers and those who have intercourse with males, and the rest of the very grievous sins which are deserving of death,--if it becomes him who is an man of the

world, to have done this, much more then have the Ineffable and the First Mystery, who are the lords of the universe, the authority to act in all things as it pleases them, that they forgive every one who shall receive mysteries.

"Or if on the other hand a king to-day invests a soldier with a royal vesture and sends him into foreign regions, and he commits murders and other grievous sins which are deserving of death, then they will not impute them to him, and are not able to do him any evil because he is invested with the royal vesture,--how much more then those who wear the mysteries of the vestures of the Ineffable and those of the First Mystery, who are lords over all those of the height and all those of the depth!"

Jesus tries Kayapaa. Thereafter Jesus saw an woman who came to make repentance. He had baptized her three times, and yet she had not done what was worthy of the baptisms. And the Saviour desired to try Kayapaa, to see if he was compassionate and forgiving, as he had commanded them. He said to Kayapaa: "Lo, three times have I baptized this soul, and yet at this third time she has not done what is worthy of the mysteries of the Light. Wherefor then cloth she make her body good for nothing? Now, therefore, Kayapaa, perform the mystery which cuts off the souls from the inheritances of the Light; perform that mystery in order that it may cut off the soul of this woman from the Inheritance of the Light."
When then the Saviour had said this, he tried [Kayapaa] to see whether he was compassionate and forgiving.
When then the Saviour had said this, Kayapaa

said: "My Adanay, let her yet this time, that we may give her the higher mysteries; and if she is fit, then have you let her inherit the Light-kingdom, but if she is not fit, then have you [to] cut her off from the Light-kingdom."
When then Kayapaa had said this, the Saviour knew that Kayapaa was compassionate as he and forgiving.
When then all this was said, the Saviour said to his disciples: "Have you understood all these words and the type of this woman?"

Marayam interprets the incident from a former saying. Marayam answered and said: "My Adanay, I have understood the mysteries of the things which have fallen to this woman's lot. Concerning the things then which have fallen to her lot, you have spoken to us aforetime in similitude, saying: 'An man owned a fig-tree in his vineyard; and he came to look for its fruit, and he found not a single one on it. He said to the vine-dresser: Lo, three years do I come to look for fruit on this fig-tree, and I have not any produce at all from it. Cut it down then; why does it make the ground also good for nothing? But he answered and said to him: My lord, have patience with it still this year, until I dig round it and give it dung; and if it bears in another year, you have let it, but if you do not find any fruit] at all, then have you [to] cut it down.' Lo, my Adanay, this is the solution of the word."
The Saviour answered and said to Marayam: Well said, spiritual one]. This is [the solution of] the word."
Marayam continued again and said to the Saviour: "My Adanay, an man who has received mysteries and has not done what is worthy of

them, but he has turned and has sinned, thereafter he has again repented and has been in great repentance,--is it then lawful for my brethren to renew for him the mystery which he has received, or rather give him a mystery out of the lower mysteries,--is it lawful, or not?"

In the case of repentance only higher mysteries than those previously received can remit sins. The Saviour answered and said to Marayam: "Aman, amen, I say to you: Neither the mystery which he has received, nor the lower hearken to him, to forgive his sins; but it is the mysteries which are higher than those which he has received, which hearken to him and forgive his sins. Now, therefore, Marayam, let your brethren give him the mystery which is higher than that which he has received, and they are to accept his repentance from him and forgive his sins,--the latter indeed, because he has received it once more, and the former, because he has towered over them [the lower mysteries] upward,--the latter indeed hearkens not to him to forgive his sin; but it is the mystery which is higher than that which he has received, that forgives his sins. But if on the other hand he has received the three mysteries in the two spaces or in the third from within, and he has turned and transgressed, no mystery hearkens to him to help him in his repentance, neither the higher nor the lower, save the mystery of the First Mystery and the mysteries of the Ineffable,--it is they which hearken to him and accept his repentance from him."
Marayam answered and said: "My Adanay, an man who has received mysteries up to two or three in the second or third space, and he has not transgressed, but is still in his faith in uprightness
and without play-acting, [what will befall him]?"

There is no limit to the number of mysteries the faithful may receive. And the Saviour answered and said to Marayam: Every man who has received mysteries in the second and in the third space, and has not transgressed, but is still in his faith without play-acting, it is lawful for such an one to receive mysteries in the space which pleases him, from the first to the last, because they have not transgressed."

Marayam continued again and said: "My Adanay, an man who has known the godhead and has received of the mysteries of the Light, and has turned and transgressed and done lawlessly and has not turned to repent, and an man on the other hand who has not found the godhead nor known it, and that man is a sinner and moreover impious, and they both have come out of the body,--which of them will get more suffering in the judgments?"

The fate of the gnostic who sins is more terrible than that of the ignorant sinner. The Saviour answered again and said to Marayam: "Aman, amen, I say to you: The man who has known the godhead and has received the mysteries of the Light, and sinned and has not turned to repent, he will get suffering in the chastisements of the judgments in great sufferings and judgments exceedingly far more in comparison with the impious and breaking man who has not known the godhead. Now, therefore, who has ears to hear, let him hear."

Marayam interprets the same from a former saying. When then the Saviour had said this, Marayam started forward and said: "My Adanay, my lightman has ears, and I have understood the whole word which you have spoken. Concerning this word then you have spoken to us in a similitude:

'The slave who knew the will of his lord and made not ready nor did the will of his lord, will receive great blows; but he who knew not and did not, will be deserving of less. For from every one to whom more is entrusted, of him will more be demanded, and to whom much is handed over, of him much is required,'--that is, my Adanay: He who knew the godhead and has found the mysteries of the Light and has transgressed, will be chastized in a far greater chastisement than he who has not known the godhead. This, my Adanay, is the solution of the word."

Marayam continued again and said to the Saviour: "My Adanay, if the faith and the mysteries shall have revealed themselves,--now, therefore, if souls come into the world in many circuits and are neglectful of receiving mysteries, hoping that, if they come into the world at any other circuit, they will receive them, will they not then be in danger of not succeeding in receiving the mysteries?"

Of those who procrastinate, saying they have many births before them. The Saviour answered and said to his disciples: "Herald to the whole world and say to men: Strive thereafter that you may receive the mysteries of the Light in this time of affliction and enter into the Light-kingdom. Join not one day to another, or one circuit to another, hoping that you may succeed in receiving the mysteries if you come into the world in another circuit.

"And these know not when the number of the perfect souls will be at hand; for if the number of the perfect souls shall be at hand, I will now shut the gates of the Light, and no one from this hour onwards will enter in, nor will

any one hereafter go forth, for the number of the perfect souls is completed and the mystery of the First Mystery is completed, for the sake of which the universe has arisen,--that is: I am that Mystery.

Of the time of the completion. "And from this hour onwards no one will be able to enter into the Light and no one be able to go forth. For at the completion of the time of the number of the perfect souls, before I have set fire to the world, in order that it may purify the aeons and the veils and the firmaments and the whole earth and also all the matters which are on it, mankind will be still existing.

Those who procrastinate are excluded from the Light. "At that time then the faith will reveal itself still more and the mysteries in those days. And many souls will come by means of the circuits of the changes of the body, and coming back into the world are some of those in this present time who have hearkened to me, how I taught, who at the completion of the number of the perfect souls will find the mysteries of the Light and receive them and come to the gates of the Light and find that the number of the perfect souls is complete, which is the completion of the First Mystery and the gnosis of the universe. And they will find that I have shut the gates of the Light and that it is impossible that any one should enter in or that any one should go forth from this hour.

Their entreaties at the gates of Light. "Those souls then will knock at the gates of the Light, saying: Adanay, open to us! And I will answer to them: I know you not, from where you are. And they will say to me: We have received of your mysteries and fulfilled your whole teaching and you have taught us on the high

ways. And I will answer and say to them: I know you not, who you are, you who are doers of iniquity and of evil even to now. Wherefor go into the outer darkness. And from that hour they will go into the outer darkness, there where is howling and grinding of teeth.

"For this cause then, herald to the whole world and say to them: 'Strive thereafter, to renounce the whole world and the whole matter therein, that you may receive the mysteries of the Light before the number of the perfect souls is completed, in order that they may not make you stop before the gates of the Light and. lead you away into the outer darkness.'
"Now, therefore, who has ears to hear, let him hear."

Marayam interprets the same. When then the Saviour had said this, Marayam started forward again and said: "My Adanay, not only has my lightman ears, but my soul has heard and understood all the words which you say. Now, therefore, my Adanay, concerning the words which you have spoken: 'Herald to the men of the world and say to them: Strive thereafter, to receive the mysteries of the Light, in this time of affliction, that you may inherit the Light-kingdom....
